quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which traffic signal?
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: To prepare for hazards on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Maintain focus toward the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.
questions.explanation: Good drivers spot problems early by looking ahead and to the sides. Don't just stare straight. Scan the whole road and roadside.

questions.question: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel when driving?
questions.explanation: Place your hands at 2 and 10 o'clock on the steering wheel. This position gives you the best control and lets you turn quickly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you a roundabout is coming. Enter at low speed and let other traffic go first.

questions.question: You should not try to drive next to a large truck in a roundabout.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take up multiple lanes in a roundabout. Do not drive beside them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the divider ahead.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.
Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. Passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: Never drive through, around, or under any railroad gate or barrier.
questions.explanation: Do not drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers. It is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Be sure the passing lane is clear.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Check that the passing lane is empty before you pass. Signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you face a green light but traffic blocks the intersection, you should:

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter if traffic blocks the intersection. If you get stuck there when the light turns red, you will block other traffic and get a ticket.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: One lane is ending. Move left to merge with traffic.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: One lane is ending. Move left to merge with traffic.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that a lane is ending soon. You must merge left with the other traffic.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely:
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to a blind person using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and look both ways before proceeding carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When driving near children playing, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run into the street without looking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run into the street without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful around children. They may not understand danger and can run out in front of your car without warning.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on highways can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly makes drivers behind you frustrated and more likely to pass dangerously. Drive with traffic flow at the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, remember:

options.text: Roads are slippery when rain first starts.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after rain starts. Your tires lose grip on the wet surface. Slow down and give yourself more space to stop.

questions.question: What does a dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass, even if it is not safe.
You can pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When a car is entering the interstate from a ramp into your lane, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get ahead of them.
Honk your horn to warn them.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.
Change lanes to let them merge safely, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them merge safely, if possible.
questions.explanation: Help drivers entering the highway merge smoothly. Change lanes when you can to give them safe space.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This diamond-shaped yellow warning sign tells you that the divided highway is about to end and you will soon face oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If an oncoming car's headlights are too bright, you should:

options.text: Look at the center of the road.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If bright headlights are coming toward you, look to the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your side of the road. Do not flash your bright lights back.

questions.question: When you see an accident ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived.

questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Keep your attention on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to an accident, fire, or disaster just to look.

questions.question: You are driving at night and a car is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On either high or low beam.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when a car is coming toward you or when you are following another car at night. Switch to low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.question: When you see a red traffic light flashing, you must:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Yield to all traffic and pedestrians, then go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices turn off.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about dangers ahead. This sign warns that the road curves to the right.

questions.question: You are driving on a city street and see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as few times as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down to a stop.
Turn on flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down to a stop.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows, do not hit the brakes right away. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by releasing the accelerator. Once you are going very slowly, gently brake and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. You can turn in the direction the arrow points, but first yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about dangers ahead. This sign warns that you are leaving a one-way highway and will soon drive on a two-way highway with traffic in both directions.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Having a driver license is a:
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege that you must earn and keep. It is not a right.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Is less dangerous when drinking beer instead of wine.
Is less dangerous when drinking wine instead of beer.
Is most dangerous when drinking hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol hurt your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: This yellow warning sign means:

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive with caution, and watch for children.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed on roads near schools. It warns drivers to slow down, be careful, and watch for children.

questions.question: When passing an animal being driven, ridden, or led on a public road, drivers should:

options.text: Drive next to the animal for as long as possible.

questions.explanation: Slow down and drive carefully when you see animals on the road. It is illegal to purposefully scare an animal being ridden, driven, or led on or near a public road.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road. This helps you avoid being blinded by the oncoming lights.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all corners, yield to any driver:
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles move through in the order they arrived. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the right goes first.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in the lane you want to enter. Make sure no other drivers are moving into the same spot.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left. What should you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until there are no vehicles before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Other vehicles proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: You are too drowsy to drive safely. What should you do?

options.text: Open all the windows and turn on the air conditioning.
Talk to a friend on the phone.

questions.explanation: When tired, you cannot drive safely. Your reactions slow down and your decision-making skills decrease. Leave the road and rest.

questions.question: How do you properly enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and merge at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and merge at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal and merge at the same speed as traffic. Always yield to other vehicles when entering a roadway.

questions.question: What do orange signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Orange signs are work zone signs. They are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols and warn that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: Which is not a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic must keep to the right.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes. Stay in the right lane if moving slower than other traffic. If you miss your exit, proceed to the next one. Do not back up or make a U-turn on interstates.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving. You have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. Treat them like stop signs.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: If power steering fails, you will need extra effort to steer. Reduce your speed and drive to a safe area to stop.

questions.question: You see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you of workers, slow-moving equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets and roads where you cannot enter. You may see it if you try to go the wrong way on an expressway ramp.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, how can you avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right?
questions.explanation: On an interstate highway, watch for upcoming on-ramps. When safe, move to the left lane to let vehicles enter from the on-ramps on your right.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle or property, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to the vehicle or property you hit.

questions.question: If you are following a distracted driver, you should:
questions.explanation: Allow extra space if you think the driver ahead may be distracted. Distracted driving causes many collisions. Extra following distance can help prevent a crash.

questions.question: As you near an intersection, the traffic light turns from green to yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Apply the brakes sharply to stop.
Be prepared to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be prepared to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Be ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: You may drive slower than the posted speed limit based on road conditions. Reduced speed is needed for safety on curves, hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, and roads with animals or pedestrians.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull off the road. Passing on the right is only allowed if you can do it without leaving the roadway.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road surface. How do you prevent it in rainy weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: In rainy weather, drive slower to reduce hydroplaning risk. Driving too fast causes tires to ride on water and lose contact with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: You approach a green traffic light, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.
Don't enter until you can get completely across.
Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter until you can get completely across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection unless you can get completely across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection is illegal.
